newsitem.title: UK: Rain halts UK barley harvest, dry weather ahead.
newsitem.headline: Rain halts UK barley harvest, dry weather ahead.

text.p: Wet weather in much of England has brought the barley harvest to a halt, analysts said.
But better conditions over the weekend could make it possible for combines to start moving again.
Although there were showers on Friday in the east and south-east, the rain was mostly light, a spokesman for the London Weather Centre said.
Southern England was likely to see clear weather from Saturday, lasting possibly into Wednesday, the spokesman said.

"Everything's so damp," a specialist at the ADAS agricultural advisory service complained. Less than ten per cent of the barley had been harvested so far, he said. Good progress had been made in the south and, particularly, south-west, with some work started in the counties to the north of London.
Repoerted yields varied widely, he said. Early cuts had been off light land and had given dismal figures. But more recent harvesting had given better numbers.
He suspected that yields overall might be a bit down, for the crop as a whole, but increased area made a bigger total crop likely.
According to ministry estimates the UK's barley crop was 7.78 million tonnes in 1996.
